messages:
sam: Thinking about adding a "per-route routing cost preview" to the console — basically show expected unit cost delta if we change routing policy for a tenant. quick mock: https://img.redwood/mock/routing-cost :eyes:
neha: love the idea. question: should the preview simulate cache hit-rate changes too? prefetch/shared-cache effects can swing unit costs a lot.
mia: we need to be careful — previews that assume 100% caching are misleading. propose two modes: steady-state (post-warm) and cold-start (first-1000 requests) so customers see a range.
nashley: +1 for ranges. UX Q: where does this live? under model rollouts or quota settings?
sam: thinking a little panel on rollout page and a toggle in quota/route editor — same backend calc. UX should show per-token, per-invocation, and amortized cost.
leo: backend note: to simulate, we need historical prefix-shape distribution and our cache crediting algorithm. we could run a lightweight sampling job over the tenant's last 7 days. cost estimate = baseline_unit_cost * routing_multiplier - cache_savings_estimate.
neha: for cache_savings_estimate, we'd need to attribute prefix hits to routes. current telemetry tags only have model_name and route_id, not routing_decision. we should add a token-level tag `routing_decision` and `cache_hit:true/false`.
ops-bot: deploy queued: add-telemetry-routing-decision -> infra/staging (ETA 18:00)
mia: nice. small API contract suggestion: preview endpoint /api/v1/preview/routing-cost with body {"route_from":"r1","route_to":"r2","window_days":7,"mode":"steady|cold"}. response: {"token_cost":..., "cache_savings":..., "per_model_breakdown": [...]} — keep it simple.
neha: agree on API. implementation detail: per_model_breakdown should include model_sku and quantization profile, otherwise numbers are useless.
nashley: product question for @product-lily — will customers understand amortized vs marginal? want labels and default to "expected per-invocation" with a little tooltip.
product-lily: i can draft microcopy. please include an example: "Switching 10% of traffic to model-x reduces average cost by 3% but increases 99th p latency by 20ms" — that makes tradeoffs tangible.
sam: good call. also add a small "what changed" diff between current routing and simulated routing: expected QPS redistribution, and top-3 routes impacted.
leo: telemetry cost: tagging every token adds cardinality. suggest we add tags only for sampled requests used by the preview job; rest keep low-cardinality metrics. sampling job will run with deterministic hash so previews are stable.
neha: sampling is fine but preview accuracy suffers if sample misses rare but expensive promptshapes. maybe preview UI should show a confidence band and sample coverage.
mia: +1 show confidence band. also add a checkbox "include prefetch/shared-cache effects" with explanation: "Estimates assume shared prefix cache is split per route proportionally" — we need to be transparent.
nashley: rollout plan? dev -> staging -> canary. canary includes a few large tenants. we should provide a 'preview-as' feature so SRE can run the preview for tenant X before toggling routing.
leo: will add endpoints and a background job to re-run previews daily for tenants with heavy changes. store last_preview_ts.
neha: one more: billing implications. preview could be misinterpreted as guaranteed saving. add a legal disclaimer and a small "expected variance" percentage.
product-lily: i'll work with legal and design. will mock microcopy and tooltip text.
sam: dev tasks: 1) add telemetry tags (routing_decision, cache_hit) 2) preview API + sampling job 3) UI panel + microcopy 4) canary + release notes. timeline?
leo: can do (1) and (2) in 2 sprints. sampling infra mostly exists.
mia: UI mock in 1 sprint. canary rollout + docs next sprint.
neha: I'll own QA for cache attribution accuracy and produce a quick A/B check: run preview vs observed cost after a small controlled reroute.
nashley: awesome. small follow-up: include an export CSV for finance teams with per-model/unit econ. they love spreadsheets. :moneybag:
sam: noted. thanks folks. will file tasks and a short RFC. tagging follow-ups: @product-lily for microcopy, @leo for infra, @neha for QA. :thumbsup:
